episodes.title: Everything Wrong With Scientology
episodes.description:
Unfiltered deep dive the of the secrets of Scientology. Please don't sue me. But this weird religion has gotten attention recently because of the Scientology speedrun trend that has young people storming into Church of Scientology buildings in goofy outfits to see how far they can get before staff throw them out, and the running joke is that the second floor unlocks Tom Cruise as a final boss. In this video I explain what Scientology actually is, where it came from, and why it is one of the most controversial organisations on the planet. We start with founder L Ron Hubbard, the pulp science fiction writer who created Dianetics in 1950 and turned it into a religion in 1953, then cover the core belief in an immortal alien spirit called a thetan, the auditing process and the E meter, the Bridge to Total Freedom and how much it really costs to reach Clear and Operating Thetan, and the secret OT III story of the galactic overlord Xenu. From there we get into the controversies, including the Fair Game policy, Suppressive Persons and disconnection, the harassment of journalist Paulette Cooper and Operation Freakout, Operation Snow White and the largest infiltration of the United States government in history, the death of Lisa McPherson, the Sea Org and the compound known as The Hole, leader David Miscavige and the disappearance of his wife Shelly, the Narconon drug rehab network, and why celebrities like Tom Cruise and John Travolta are so central to the church. I also cover Anonymous and Project Chanology, the war on psychiatry, and the pyramid style money structure behind all of it. Finally I explain why the exact same organisation is a tax exempt religion in America but a convicted fraud in France and an unrecognised commercial enterprise in Germany, and why that contrast says something important about how a strong regulated European state protects its citizens. Is storming Scientology buildings justified, is Scientology a cult, and is it even a religion at all. Let me know what you think in the comments.
